title: macOS: Embedded game process is shown as "Not Responding" in Activity Monitor
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot 4.7.1.stable.official [a13da4feb].
- Earlier versions not tested.

### System information

Godot v4.7.1.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.5.2) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Apple M4 - Apple M4 (10 threads) - 32.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When a project is run from the macOS editor with **Embed Game on Next Play** enabled, Mac OS Activity Monitor marks the child debug game process as **Godot (Not Responding)**. The embedded game continues to render and respond to input, so it does not appear to be actually hung. The editor process itself is not marked as unresponsive.

This reproduces in a brand-new project containing only a Node2D main scene, with no scripts, plugins, GDExtensions, or project-specific logic. The affected child process is launched with the `--embedded` command-line argument.

Expected behavior: Activity Monitor should report the embedded debug game process as responsive while it is running and accepting input.

This appears distinct from #106379 / #106614, which concerned uncapped OpenGL frame rate for embedded games and was fixed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the official Godot 4.7.1 macOS editor.
2. Create a new project using the Compatibility renderer.
3. Add a Node2D as the root node, save the scene, and set it as the main scene. No script is required.
4. Ensure **Embed Game on Next Play** is enabled (the default).
5. Run the project from the editor (for example with Command+B or the Run Project button).
6. Open macOS Activity Monitor and select the CPU tab.
7. Observe that the child Godot process for the embedded game is labeled **Godot (Not Responding)**, even though the embedded game remains interactive.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A — reproducible in a brand-new project with only an empty Node2D main scene.
